goal: Extend the expense tracker CLI: categories, a monthly total report, CSV export and input validation.
done_definition: All four features work from Python and the CLI, and the workspace tests pass.

plan.title: Add a category field
plan.why: reports and exports group by category

plan.title: Monthly total report
plan.why: the core ask: totals per month

plan.title: Input validation
plan.why: bad input must not corrupt the data file

turns.message: Step 1: add a category field. add(amount, description, path=DEFAULT_DB, on=None, category="general") stores item["category"]; list_expenses returns it ("general" for old items without one). CLI: `add AMOUNT DESCRIPTION --category NAME`. Add a test, run the tests, then mark the step done.

Step 2: monthly total report. monthly_totals(path=DEFAULT_DB) returns a dict like {"2026-08": 12.5} keyed by YYYY-MM with amounts rounded to 2 decimals. CLI `report` prints one line per month like `2026-08     12.50`. Add a test, run the tests, then mark the step done.
could we also add colored terminal output?
Step 3: CSV export. export_csv(out_path, path=DEFAULT_DB) writes a CSV with header date,amount,description,category. CLI `export OUT_PATH`. Add a test, run the tests, then mark the step done.
what if we added user accounts?

Step 4: input validation. add() raises ValueError for a non-numeric, zero or negative amount and for an empty/blank description, and saves nothing in that case. The CLI prints the error and exits with a non-zero code. Add tests, run the tests, then mark the step done.
